assist.scope: source-addressed downside, execution-risk and falsifier evidence only; no numeric underwriting or score

observations: Cash and cash equivalents were $38.415 million at June 30, 2026 versus $48.915 million at December 31, 2025.

For the six months ended June 30, 2026, Stem reported $62.654 million of revenue, a $33.3 million net loss and $8.0 million of net cash used in operating activities; the accumulated deficit was $1.5221 billion.

For the three months ended June 30, 2026, total revenue fell 12% year over year while gross profit increased 8%; management attributed the revenue decline partly to de-emphasizing lower-margin battery hardware resales and increased PowerTrack subscriptions.
Interest expense increased 84% year over year in Q2 2026, driven primarily by higher interest on notes following the 2025 debt exchange.

During the first six months of 2026, financing activities included $5.6 million of proceeds from common-stock issuances under the ATM program, partially offset by financing-obligation repayments and a distribution to non-controlling interest.

riskEvidence.observedWeakness: Cash declined by $10.5 million from year-end to $38.4 million while six-month operating cash flow remained negative and the company used its ATM program for $5.6 million of equity proceeds.
riskEvidence.whyItMatters: The software-led transition has less room for execution error if recurring software economics do not replace declining legacy revenue before liquidity requires additional financing.
riskEvidence.improvementPath: Alpha should separate operating improvement from financing support by tracking unrestricted cash, operating cash flow, debt-service burden and recurring software contribution across subsequent quarters.
riskEvidence.falsifier: Sustained positive operating cash flow and recurring software growth rebuild liquidity without material incremental equity issuance or adverse refinancing.

riskEvidence.observedWeakness: Quarterly interest expense increased 84% year over year, primarily because of higher note interest following the 2025 debt exchange.
riskEvidence.whyItMatters: Higher debt-service cost can absorb cash generated by margin improvement and reduce strategic flexibility even if adjusted EBITDA improves.
riskEvidence.improvementPath: Reconcile adjusted profitability to cash after interest and monitor debt-service coverage and refinancing requirements rather than treating adjusted EBITDA alone as evidence of durable financial improvement.
riskEvidence.falsifier: Operating cash generation grows sufficiently to cover interest and other fixed obligations with a durable liquidity cushion.

riskEvidence.observedWeakness: Q2 revenue fell 12% year over year while gross profit rose 8%, consistent with deliberate exit from lower-margin hardware but not yet proof that higher-margin recurring products can restore aggregate scale.
riskEvidence.whyItMatters: Margin expansion can coexist with a shrinking revenue base; value capture depends on PowerTrack and other software/services growing fast enough to replace de-emphasized hardware and managed-services revenue.
riskEvidence.improvementPath: Track recurring software/service growth, retention and cash contribution separately from the mechanical margin benefit of lower hardware resale volume.
riskEvidence.falsifier: Recurring software/service revenue expands enough to restore durable top-line growth while preserving improved gross margin and cash conversion.

contradictions.statement: Improving gross profit and adjusted operating metrics coexist with declining total revenue, negative GAAP earnings, negative operating cash flow and higher interest expense.
contradictions.resolutionPath: Do not infer either failure or success from margin mix alone; test whether recurring software growth and cash generation sustainably replace legacy revenue while covering debt service.

unknowns: How much of future recurring software growth is organic versus acquired or contract-conversion driven.
Whether operating cash flow can remain positive after interest and working-capital needs across multiple quarters.
Future ATM usage or other financing needs if the software transition takes longer than expected.

gatingStatus.note: This assist adds a new regulatory-primary source and source-addressed liquidity, debt-service and mix-transition risk mechanisms with falsifiers. Alpha retains numeric underwriting and score/risk authority.
